newsitem.title: CHINA: SHANGHAI B SHARES END DOWN, ERASING MORNING GAINS.
newsitem.headline: SHANGHAI B SHARES END DOWN, ERASING MORNING GAINS.

text.p: Shanghai's foreign currency B shares edged down on Thursday in stable trading, erasing morning gains, brokers said.
The B share market had gained in Thursday morning trading on buying of recently listed issues, including Shanghai Zhenhua Port Machinery Co Ltd and Hainan Airlines Co, they said.
However, the B index slipped 0.121 points or 0.16 percent to 74.182 at the close on moderate turnover of $7.132 million, compared with $9.841 million on Wednesday.
Selective purchases -- including institutional buying of Zhenhua Port -- failed to keep the market in positive territory in the afternoon but the short-term outlook remained strong, brokers said.
"The B shares were relatively stable and turnover was very light," said an analyst at Shenyin & Wanguo Securities.
"Trading will be stable in the short term and I don't expect any bad news," he said.
Investors were waiting for more 1997 interim results ahead of the deadline at the end of August before returning to the market in force, brokers said.
In the longer term, investors are looking toward a five-yearly Communist Party congress in September or October in expectation of new economic policies that would benefit listed firms, they said.
Of 46 B shares, 42 traded with 15 down, 16 up and 11 unchanged.
Shanghai Yaohua Pilkington Glass Co was the biggest B share loser on speculative selling, plunging $0.030 or 9.09 percent to $0.300.

Zhenhua Port, which listed earlier this week, was the most actively traded share and the top gainer in a falling market. The stock surged $0.052 or 9.85 percent to $0.580 on volume of around 2.1 million shares.
Shanghai Chlor Alkali Chemical Co was the second biggest gainer, soaring $0.022 or 9.17 percent to $0.262.
Chlor Alkali has benefited from speculation that it would merge with a petrochemical company, although the firm has denied such rumours in the past, brokers said.

Domestic currency A shares reversed early losses on buying of companies that have H shares listed in Hong Kong, brokers said. H shares, shares of Chinese firms listed in Hong Kong, have recently performed strongly, they said.
The A share index jumped 29.390 points or 2.40 percent to 1,255.191 points on turnover of 3.074 billion yuan against 2.788 billion on Wednesday.
The SSE30 blue chip rose 61.517 points or 1.67 percent to 3,749.004 points.
Brokers said the B share market would probably continue to trade in a narrow range on Friday but with a positive tone.
